notes: Simple two-node parallel ladder. Net map: n1 = left corner node between the + terminal of V-DC 6 (100 V) and the left lead of the series Resistor 3 (10 ohm) -- the short vertical at x~76 from the top of the source up to the top rail at y~190; n2 = top rail at y~188 running from the right lead of Resistor 3 (x~204) rightward, T-ing down to the top of I-DC 0 (x~231), the top of Resistor 2 (10 ohm, x~293), the top of Inductor 4 (0.5 H, x~355), and turning down at the top-right corner (x~430) to the upper plate of Capacitor 1 (5 mF); 0 = bottom rail at y~315 (slightly sloped, y~322 at the left end) joining the - terminal of V-DC 6, the bottom of I-DC 0, the bottom of Resistor 2, the bottom of Inductor 4, the lower plate of Capacitor 1, and GND 5, which hangs below the rail on the continuation of the Resistor 2 leg at x~305. Judgment calls: (a) verified at 5-7x that the top rail is one unbroken run -- all four downward branches are plain T-junctions, there are no crossovers or hops anywhere in this drawing, so nothing had to be split; (b) the Resistor 2 leg passes through the bottom rail and continues down to the GND symbol, i.e. the rail/leg intersection at (305,317) is a junction, which is what makes the whole bottom rail net 0; (c) Capacitor 1 is physically vertical (two horizontal plates) even though its bbox is wider than tall, so its terminals are ordered top-then-bottom like the other vertical parts; (d) 2-terminal order convention used throughout: index 0 = top (or left for the horizontal Resistor 3), index 1 = bottom (or right); V-DC 6 index 0 is the + plate, drawn uppermost; I-DC 0 arrow points up, index 0 is its top lead; (e) bootstrap values were largely wrong (R3 right lead was 0, inductor and I-DC had a phantom net n3) -- the partition above was re-derived from the drawing.
